rules.description: Fail when a failed operation is disguised as a successful default or empty result. Pass when failure is explicit and distinguishable from a legitimate empty result. A documented optional capability returning an explicit unavailable result is valid.

Fail when production code promises an effect it cannot perform, including a stub, fake implementation or unreachable promised branch. Pass when it does the promised work or returns an explicit unsupported/error result. Abstract declarations and deliberate, documented no-ops are valid.

Fail when a production path presents invented examples, fixtures or canned responses as actual results. Pass when the result comes from its stated source. Mocks and synthetic data within test boundaries are valid; examples clearly labelled as examples are valid.

Fail when an error provides neither a useful cause nor a way to fix or investigate it. Pass when the caller receives the failed operation and a concrete remedy or diagnostic reference. Do not reveal source content, credentials or private provider output to make an error more descriptive.

Fail when a nontrivial domain threshold, limit or unit conversion has no name, units or explanation. Pass when its meaning and units are clear from a named constant or domain value. Ordinary indices, zero/one identities and values intrinsic to an independently specified algorithm are valid.

Fail when a function's name promises behavior or an effect it does not have, or hides a materially different effect. Pass when its name describes its actual result and effects in context. Established API names may be kept when their contract is clear.
